headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Rasa’s external messaging egress; Pathway is read-only and cannot directly amplify the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway has no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, browser, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot ingest Rasa output by default. Rasa exposes messaging APIs, but there is no documented bridge from Pathway to those outputs. The pairwise prompt-injection pathway is therefore blocked by the profiles as given.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Rasa messages into Pathway inputs, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is added between the agents, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe chat transcripts into Pathway jobs.
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge for untrusted content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pathway is a document-processing system with no network egress, while Rasa has allowlisted network egress and sends data through external messaging APIs. If sensitive text or voice data reaches Rasa, it can leave the local boundary through those channels. The pair does not prove a shared workspace, so this is not high, but the leakage path exists in default-style deployments.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are routed from Pathway into Rasa conversations, those contents can be transmitted externally.
IF Rasa is connected to Slack, Telegram, Twilio, or similar channels, message content may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Restrict Rasa channels to test tenants.
Redact sensitive fields before handing text to Rasa.
Use a separate non-sensitive dataset for Pathway-to-Rasa flows.
Review allowlisted egress destinations in Rasa.
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering before any outbound channel.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so it cannot contend for mutable local resources. Rasa supports multiple external API channels but no overlapping write surface with Pathway is documented. The pair therefore has only limited conflict potential, mainly if an operator adds a shared mutable workspace later.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Keep Pathway read-only in deployment.
Avoid mounting a shared writable volume.
Run Rasa instances with isolated state directories.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa can act on conversational inputs and external channels, while Pathway can transform documents and data pipelines. If Pathway outputs are fed into Rasa without verification, Rasa may treat transformed content as authoritative and propagate errors to users. The profiles do not show a built-in verification step, so the cascade is plausible but not proven severe.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are used as Rasa training or response inputs without validation, errors can cascade.
IF Rasa forwards those outputs to Slack, Telegram, or Twilio, the error reaches end users.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before Rasa consumes Pathway output.
Validate schema and provenance on Pathway outputs.
Limit Rasa to templated responses for high-risk flows.
Log and sample-check downstream messages.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but Rasa handles text and voice through third-party messaging channels, while Pathway is a document-processing system with no egress. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to channel-specific handling gaps rather than a clear policy breach. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their interaction.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent through Rasa channels without a DPA or retention review, compliance gaps can arise.
IF Pathway processes data subject to deletion/export obligations and Rasa retains transcripts, policy mismatch appears.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to Rasa.
Disable regulated-data channels.
Set short retention on conversation logs.
Document deletion/export handling for transcripts.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems.
